claim: The front fits three cards I know: this one, saa-1 in the extras, and chapter-2-extras/saa-wakarimasen, and nothing says which one is wanted.
evidence: Production front: 'Well... / I don't know. casual style' (answer さあ). saa-1 Production front: 'Well... I don't know. casual style' (answer さあ、わからない). chapter-2-extras/saa-wakarimasen: さあ、わかりません | 'Well, I don't know.'
fix: Gloss the single word as 'Well... (hesitating; I don't know)' or add a hint like 'the hesitation word alone' so it no longer reads as the whole sentence saa-1 asks for.

claim: ね alone (chapter-6/ne-particle) also means 'isn't it?' and this unit's own note says an い-adjective takes ね directly in casual speech, so ね is a correct answer to this front that the card marks wrong.
evidence: Production front: '..., isn't it? (casual, seeking agreement) casual style', answer だね. chapter-6/ne-particle: ね | 'Right?, isn't it? (particle)'. na-adjective-casual-ne-kirei note: 'An い-adjective takes ね directly (おおきいね).'
fix: Say on the front what comes before it, e.g. 'after a noun or な-adjective: ..., isn't it? (casual)'.

claim: よ alone (chapter-12/yo-particle-emphasis) is the emphasis particle I already know, and an い-adjective takes it directly in casual speech, so よ fits this front as well as だよ.
evidence: Production front: '..., you know. (casual, adding emphasis) casual style', answer だよ. chapter-12/yo-particle-emphasis: よ | 'Emphasis particle (calls attention to new information)'. na-adjective-casual-yo-kirei note: 'An い-adjective takes よ directly (おおきいよ).'
fix: Say on the front what comes before it, e.g. 'after a noun or な-adjective: ..., you know (casual)'.

claim: Calling って a 'contraction' of は reads as doubtful: the two share no sound, and nothing I was taught explains how one shortens into the other.
evidence: Answer: 'Casual contraction of は (topic marker in a casual question).' Note: 'In casual speech は is often dropped and sometimes becomes って'.
fix: Say that って can stand in for は in casual speech, without calling it a contraction.

claim: The bracket on the English front spells out the exact construction the card tests (add だ before ね), so the front gives the answer away.
evidence: Production front: 'It's pretty, isn't it? (な-adjective + だ before casual ね) casual style'.
fix: Move the bracketed rule to the note and leave 'It's pretty, isn't it?' with the casual style hint on the front.

claim: The bracket on the English front spells out the exact construction the card tests (add だ before よ), so the front gives the answer away.
evidence: Production front: 'It's pretty, you know. (な-adjective + だ before casual よ) casual style'.
fix: Move the bracketed rule to the note and leave 'It's pretty, you know.' with the casual style hint on the front.

claim: The card exists to drill ちゃん, but the English front drops the suffix and gives no cue about who Hayashi is, so はやしさん or はやしくん fit just as well.
evidence: Production front: 'Family & People / Hayashi, whose is this? / casual style'. Answer: はやしちゃん、これ、だれの?
fix: Add a scene such as 'talking to a little girl named Hayashi' or put the suffix in the English ('Hayashi-chan, whose is this?').

claim: The card exists to drill くん, but the English front drops the suffix and gives no cue about who Tanaka is, so たなかさん or たなかちゃん fit just as well.
evidence: Production front: 'Family & People / Tanaka, how are you doing? / casual style'. Answer: たなかくん、げんき?
fix: Add a scene such as 'greeting a younger male colleague, Tanaka' or put the suffix in the English ('Tanaka-kun, how are you?').

claim: わからない is the plain negative of a verb, and no card before or in this chapter teaches a verb's ない form; I know only わかる, わかります and わかりません.
evidence: Answer: さあ、わからない ('Well... I don't know.'). Ledger: わかる | 'Understand (dictionary form)', わかりません | 'I don't know'. This chapter's negative cards are all adjectives or じゃない; no verb ない form appears and the card has no note.
fix: Add a note saying わからない is the casual negative of わかる (the casual form of わかりません).

claim: いかない is a verb's plain negative, which no card has taught; I know いく and いきません but not how to get from one to いかない.
evidence: Answer: おれ、いかない ('I'm not going. (male speaker)'). Ledger: いく | 'Go (dictionary form)', いいえ、いきません | 'No, (I) will not go.' No card in chapter 25 teaches a verb ない form, and this card has no note.
fix: Add a note saying いかない is the casual negative of いく (casual for いきません).

claim: '(male speaker)' does not choose between おれ and ぼく, both of which this chapter teaches as a man's casual 'I'.
evidence: Production front: 'I'm not going. (male speaker) / casual style'. Answer: おれ、いかない. pronoun-boku: 'I (casual, used mainly by men).' pronoun-ore: 'I (casual and rougher, used by men).'
fix: Make the hint name the register, e.g. 'rough male speaker' for おれ.

claim: '(casual, male speaker)' fits ぼく as well as おれ, so これ、ぼくの is as good an answer as the expected これ、おれの.
evidence: Production front: 'This is mine. (casual, male speaker) / casual style'. Answer: これ、おれの. boku-3 uses ぼくの for the same speaker type ('asked by a man, casual').
fix: Make the cue name the rougher register (e.g. 'rough male speaker') so it picks おれ over ぼく.

claim: 'asked by a man, casual' fits おれ as well as ぼく; this chapter's ore-3 gives a man おれの in the same kind of sentence.
evidence: Production front: 'Is this mine? / asked by a man, casual'. Answer: これ、ぼくの? ore-3: 'This is mine. (casual, male speaker)' → これ、おれの.
fix: Make the cue pick ぼく, e.g. 'asked by a boy' or 'a man, casual but not rough'.

claim: The scene is the same male classmate as yes-its-mine, but this card wants おれ and that one wants ぼく, with nothing on either front to tell them apart.
evidence: Production front: 'No, it's not mine. / A classmate is asked whether a pen found on the floor belongs to him.' Answer: ううん、おれのじゃない. yes-its-mine front: 'Yeah, it's mine. / A classmate confirms that a pen found on the floor is his.' Answer: うん、ぼくの.
fix: Use one pronoun for the same classmate on both cards, or add to the scene which word he uses (e.g. 'a rough-spoken classmate').

claim: Same male classmate as abe-not-mine, which wants おれ, while this card wants ぼく; the front cannot tell me which pronoun he uses.
evidence: Production front: 'Yeah, it's mine. / A classmate confirms that a pen found on the floor is his.' Answer: うん、ぼくの. abe-not-mine answer: ううん、おれのじゃない for the same scene.
fix: Use one pronoun for the classmate on both cards, or say in the scene which he uses.

claim: The front has no speaker cue at all, so ぼく, おれ, あたし or わたし (or no pronoun) all fit.
evidence: Production front: 'Work & Occupations / I'm not a teacher. / casual style'. Answer: ぼく、せんせいじゃない.
fix: Add a speaker hint, e.g. 'spoken by a man, casual', as atashi-2 and boku-3 do.

claim: The front has no speaker cue at all, so ぼく, おれ or あたし all fit, and nothing points to あたし.
evidence: Production front: 'Family & People / I'm a student, you know. / casual style'. Answer: あたし、がくせいだよ.
fix: Add 'spoken by a woman, casual' as atashi-2 does.

claim: This chapter teaches that a casual question can drop は or use って, but the front gives no cue for って, so にっこう、どんなところ? is just as right.
evidence: Production front: 'Nikko, what kind of place is it? / casual style'. Answer: にっこうって、どんなところ? casual-question-suzuki-sensei-ha-omit note: 'A casual yes/no question can drop は entirely ... Compare たなかさんってにほんじん?, where って stands in for は instead.'
fix: Add a hint naming the topic marker, e.g. 'casual, with って'.

claim: Its own note pairs it with すずきさん、せんせい?, which drops は, yet the two English fronts are built the same way, so I cannot tell which one wants って.
evidence: Production front: 'Tanaka, is he Japanese? / casual style' → たなかさんってにほんじん? casual-question-suzuki-sensei-ha-omit front: 'Suzuki, are you a teacher? / casual style' → すずきさん、せんせい?
fix: Add 'with って' to this hint and 'は dropped' to the Suzuki one.

claim: Nothing on the front asks for って, and dropping it (ラジャさん、これ、ラジャさんの?) is the pattern several other cards here use, e.g. whose-pen-question and boku-3.
evidence: Production front: 'Raja, is this yours? / casual style'. Answer: ラジャさん、これってラジャさんの? whose-pen-question: これ、だれのペン? boku-3: これ、ぼくの?
fix: Add 'casual, with って' to the hint.

claim: The note points to a card I have never seen: にっこう、きれいだね does not ship in this deck.
evidence: Note: 'Contrasts with the existing にっこう、きれいだね — same place, past tense, negated.' The only kept きれいだね sentence is kirei-dane-2: このはな、きれいだね.
fix: Point the contrast at このはな、きれいだね or at the bare きれいだね card, or drop the note.

claim: The note talks about how the deck was built ('already-used') rather than about the Japanese, and the 'paradigm' it completes mixes a house and a dog.
evidence: Note: 'Completes the i-adjective paradigm alongside the already-used あのうち、おおきくない and あのいぬ、おおきかった.'
fix: Replace with a note on the form (くない → くなかった for the past negative), or drop it.

claim: 'very' can be とても (chapter-10/totemo) as well as すごく, and nothing on the front asks for the casual すごく.
evidence: Production front: 'It was very lively. / Asked how yesterday's party was, describing the atmosphere.' Answer: すごくにぎやかだった. Ledger: とても | 'Very'.
fix: Mark the English as casual 'really' or add 'using the casual word for very' to the hint.

claim: The same words are romanized differently between the base and extras units, so I cannot tell which spelling to trust.
evidence: ううん: base casual-no 'Says: uun', extras casual-answer-no-nationality and abe-not-mine 'ūn' (which reads like a long vowel). よくない: base 'yokunai', extras ii-present-neg 'yoku nai'; おおきくない: base 'ōkikunai', extras ookii-present-neg 'ōkiku nai'. Place names: nikko-kirei-janakatta 'Nikkō' capitalized, kirei-past-aff 'hakone' lower case.
fix: Pick one spelling for each (uun, one spacing rule for adjective endings, one casing rule for place names) and apply it across both units.
